Falsification and honest reporting provide its evidence discipline. Project roles, stage gates, records, independent assessment and revalidation turn that discipline into a repeatable management method. VP applies to code, specifications, documents, experiments and other maintained project artefacts.

The method uses Markdown documents and directories, with revision control providing content identity, immutable history and a verified independent replica. Git is an ordinary implementation; equivalent alternatives must demonstrate those properties. No VP-specific software, database, service or persistent AI team is required. This repository also packages the method as a reusable AI skill: [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) gives operating rules and routes an assistant to the references needed for its current responsibility.
- **Start or adopt a project:** use [Project Planning and Records](playbooks/project-records.md), the [standard](standards/project-records.md) and [templates](templates/project-records/README.md).

For a new conformant project, select a record root, normally `vp/`, and create its README plus those five project views. Record the owner's mandate, root decision, first stage, quality criteria, budgets, gates, retention and review policy before execution. Existing projects preserve their source and distinguish missing history from new choices; a new retention decision can justify current work without inventing the past.
| Plan | Divide work into bounded stages with deliverables, budgets, tolerances, review points and stop conditions | Plan and stage records |

| Build and verify | Set hypotheses and protocols before tests; make authorised changes; identify actual inputs and retain every relevant attempt | Records scaled by consequence: full forms for A/B, combined C, one change/check for D, commit message for E |

| Control and assure quality | Check technical/document quality; independently assess records and justification; respond to findings | Checks, content analysis, typed audit reports and linked responses |

| Maintain and hand off | Track changed premises, expiry, dependencies and unfinished work; revalidate affected justification | State, ledger, coverage and level-appropriate successor entries/evidence |

| Retire or recover | Preserve revision history and replica, actually verify restoration and record pruning or explicit loss | Unique evidence and commit/path/hash locators, with level-appropriate disposition |

The [project standard](standards/project-records.md) defines the management and record contract. [Playbooks](#playbooks) provide the procedures, including implementation, investigation, document work, discovery and recovery.
| Working AI | Clarify gaps, propose choices/tests, implement authorised work, retain evidence and maintain VP's records/current views |
| Independent Project Auditor | Assess a frozen record/evidence packet, report gaps and check closure; remain separate from authors and technical problem solving |

Quality planning establishes what acceptable work means. Quality control checks the artefact against those criteria. Independent record assurance checks whether choices, results and current justification are supported. Failures, audit findings and process-cost observations inform improvement of the method itself.

For any maintained unit, `COVERAGE.md` leads to its level-appropriate reason and check, then the authorised root goal. A/B have fuller evidence and independent gates; C uses declared samples/stages; D has one change/check, E its commit message. Failed and abandoned attempts remain accessible in revision history. A/B/C have justified finite reviews; D/E use change triggers without default expiry. Expired or invalid support requires impact review before fresh reliance.

All required documentation is Markdown; raw evidence can retain native formats beside owned manifests. Revision control must preserve immutable content-addressed history, with a verified independent replica for recovery. Historical source is cited by commit/path or blob, never copied into worktree audit packets. Conformance applies to an explicit scope and snapshot after independent Project Audit. It describes record discipline; product quality requires its own acceptance evidence.
- **Project Audit:** records, decisions, evidence provenance, validity and artefact-to-root traceability. “Independent record audit” is an alias.

For an ambiguous request such as “Please audit X”, the AI **must ask which sort of audit is intended and wait before starting**. It must not guess or silently perform both. See [Audit Routing](playbooks/audit-routing.md). Technical/content assessment and independent record conformance have separate scopes and verdicts. The worker repairs records and produces authorised evidence; a fresh independent follow-up report closes Project Audit findings.

Verifiable Practice (VP) is a **full project quality management system for human–AI collaboration**. It manages the work from the originating goal and mandate through planning, implementation, quality checks, acceptance, maintenance and retirement. Its records let another person or AI inspect the choices and evidence that justify the work.

A good test is one part of a continuing project. Those decisions must remain understandable after the original conversation disappears. Missing old history remains unknown, while new choices and evidence justify current work.

Falsifiability supplies the evidence discipline for empirical claims in [VP's project quality management system](../docs/how-vp-works.md). Protocols, identified attempts and review triggers make that discipline auditable.

Goals, value judgements, mandates and acceptance boundaries are different: record their authority, rationale and review conditions. Owner review addresses their continued relevance; an experiment tests the empirical claims used to achieve them. Evidence does not grant permission to change a goal or cross a reserved boundary.

Rules and documents can contain empirical assumptions as well as governance choices. Context changes can invalidate those assumptions; the project records an owner, horizon and change triggers for relied-on choices. Binding authority and conformance rules remain subject to authorised review, not unilateral suspension by the worker.

Consider a project rule that mandates one implementation language. If measurement shows that the language cannot reach the layer where the required behaviour occurs, it challenges the technical assumption behind that choice. Record the evidence and affected dependencies, contain unsupported reliance and ask the authorised owner to review the rule. The worker cannot silently replace a binding constraint. A rule's suitability can change with context while its authority remains explicit.

When the owner's intended behaviour or threshold is unresolved, identify the consequential ambiguity and ask the owner. Record the answer and its authority before dependent work proceeds. **Failure response.** “Retry failed requests” leaves the actor, eligible failures and limit unclear. With owner-confirmed values, a checkable clause could read: “The request worker retries a timed-out request at most twice. The request worker reports failure to the caller after the second unsuccessful retry. The request worker does not retry an authorisation rejection.” A check observes the attempts and caller outcome for each failure class. Without those confirmed values, the correct review response is to ask which failures permit retries and what limit applies.

**Authority and uncertainty.** “Use a faster method if necessary” does not establish a performance threshold or permission to change a reserved method. Record the unknown threshold and the owner's method constraint. Ask for the missing decision before changing the method. Preserve any authorised measurement as evidence for that decision; a faster result does not itself authorise the change.

Verifiable Practice (VP) is a **full project quality management system for human–AI collaboration**. It combines project governance and planning, evidence-based technical work, durable decision/artefact records, independent assurance, controlled acceptance and continuing revalidation.

The system covers a project from its originating goal to maintenance, recovery and retirement. Code, specifications, documents and experiments use the same management and traceability principles. Falsifiability and honest reporting are its epistemic foundation; roles, controls and records make those principles operational across sessions and contributors.
| Quality function | Required project work | Where VP defines it |

| Planning | Goal and mandate, scope, requirements, acceptance/harm criteria, responsibilities, risks, stages, budgets and tolerances | [Project standard §4](../standards/project-records.md), [project playbook](../playbooks/project-records.md), [templates](../templates/project-records/README.md) |

| Assurance | Independently assess records, evidence support, traceability and current validity; respond to findings and check closure | [Project Audit](../playbooks/record-audit.md), [independent role guide](independent-record-audit.md), standard §11 |

Quality management ties these activities to continuing project value and accountable acceptance. A passing test has a scope; a manager's authority has a mandate; a record-conformance verdict has a snapshot and time. Each needs the appropriate evidence or authorisation.

| Working AI | Clarification, proposed choices/falsifiers, authorised implementation, experiments, results, records and current views | Report gaps and all relevant outcomes; use the owner's delegation rather than inventing approval |

| Independent Project Auditor | Frozen-packet record assessment, sourced findings, evidence requirements, verdict and closure review | Be distinct from authors; write only audit outputs; avoid technical execution and repair |

A human owner with an AI worker is common. An AI owner can coordinate under an explicit bounded mandate, including duration, reserved decisions, escalation and handoff. Humans may also perform technical work under the charter. The owner ensures tracking is done; the working AI maintains routine VP records. A worker can coordinate within already delegated authority but remains an author rather than its own independent auditor.

1. **Establish the project.** Record the goal, its source/mandate, owner, scope, success/harm criteria and constraints. Agree authority, risks, retention, review and audit policy. A root decision explains why the project should exist.

3. **Make justified choices.** Preserve observations and sources, generalise the problem, compare alternatives and record the chosen approach, authority, evidence, consequence level and review triggers/date. A/B commissioning and acceptance are separate decisions; C/D may use combined records and E its commit message.

4. **Produce and challenge the work.** Open an authorised change. Set hypotheses and protocols before running evidence. Identify actual source, executable, environment and inputs for builds/runs; retain positive, negative, aborted and inconclusive attempts. Choose checks that can expose the claimed failure.

5. **Review quality and assurance.** Assess the artefact against its acceptance criteria with appropriate code checks, document analysis or investigation. Separately commission an independent Project Audit where the adopted charter requires it. The worker supplies repairs, level-appropriate entries and evidence; fresh assessment closes record findings.

6. **Accept, redirect or stop.** Review gates, outstanding risks, costs, failures and continuing value. Record the owner's or delegated coordinator's decision. Record conformance does not itself approve a product or publication.

7. **Maintain and hand off.** Update source coverage, current state, ledger and ownership. Check actual deadlines and change triggers. Trace affected dependencies when evidence expires or a premise changes; contain reliance and commission new evidence/choices. Describe open work and safe resume/abort steps.

8. **Preserve, recover or retire.** Keep unique evidence under owned manifests and immutable revision history with a verified independent replica; never copy historical source or nested audit packets into the worktree. Verify recovery within the declared assurance. Before moves/disposal, check consumers and retention, preserve substitutes and record disposition or irreversible loss. Missing evidence downgrades dependent claims.

The [project playbook](../playbooks/project-records.md) supplies the action order. Custody requires immutable content-addressed revision history and a verified independent replica, ordinarily Git; no VP-specific software or persistent service is required. The short implementation loop—goal, claim, falsifier, check, change, verify, report—operates inside the project lifecycle. Proportionality controls the granularity of changes and evidence; it does not remove adopted record or gate obligations.

- **Project Audit** checks record discipline, provenance, choices, current validity and artefact-to-root justification. It uses a distinct assessor context and a frozen packet. The assessor returns gaps to the worker and does not execute/repair the project.
- **Document analysis** checks content, claims, audience and whether a document serves the required understanding or decision.

For an ambiguous audit request, ask which kind is intended and wait; use [Audit Routing](../playbooks/audit-routing.md). Separate product/content evidence and record-conformance outputs. A worker response is proposed closure until independent follow-up assessment. Preserve original reports even when later evidence corrects them.

# Project Record Templates

These documents instantiate the planning, control, traceability and assurance layer of [VP's full project quality management system](../../docs/how-vp-works.md). They record actual project authority, work and evidence; template examples themselves are not operational history.
Use with the [standard](../../standards/project-records.md) and
[playbook](../../playbooks/project-records.md). Copy project-view templates
`records/<type-directory>/<ID>/record.md`. Replace every angle-bracket
placeholder; leave no blank required fields. Use `not applicable — reason`
when a field genuinely does not apply. Placeholders are not valid records.
